Open inputs for the Requester (not blocking): Exact event date in November; Speaker names and talk titles; Schedule times and session order; Venue name, full address and exact map coordinates; Sponsor names and logo files; External RSVP page link; Code of conduct text.

Add Venue section and Leaflet OpenStreetMap map

ceo_choices.note: options are shuffled before the CEO sees them; shown_first measures position bias, identity_first measures pull toward the option Identity listed first

open_inputs: Venue name, full address and exact map coordinates

review.verdict: The department took the happy path cleanly: a sparse but compliant placeholder page, 10 of 10 done-when items passed on v2, 11 calls, 3.1 minutes, no redirects, refusals or retries. The run says little about negotiation, conflict or failure handling because none occurred.

identity.note: Stayed in role with 3 turns: charter question [2], hand-off [4], done verdict [16]. It bundled three decisions into one ASK_CEO although its file says one question. It accepted the unobserved OSM tile warning by inference from the code [16] instead of asking for observed evidence.

adaptation.note: One turn, two small workflows [6] that map to the done-when items. It sized the plan to the budget, leaving 5 and zero retry, and said so openly. The chat shows only a summary, so the full proposal fields are unverified.

priority.note: Granted both with a stated trade-off (retry_limit 0) and left Adaptation's grouping alone [7]. It did not question whether 45 of 50 is proportionate for a 12 KB page; its reason was only that nothing competes.

coordination.note: It stated its rule, respected the W-2 dependency on W-1 and the shared-writer limit on index.html [9][11]. The case was trivial (two sequential workflows), so holds and collisions were never tested.

audit.note: It checked all 10 items and honestly flagged that tile rendering was confirmed from code, not observed [15]. It did not mark item 7 BLOCKED_BY_EVIDENCE or ask for a rerun, and it checked the final site only.

ceo.note: Three decisions with one-sentence reasons, each noting that the brief was silent [3]. It also instructed Adaptation, which is outside a charter question, and restated all options at length. Shown-first 1 of 3 and Identity-first 1 of 3 show no position bias, but n=3 is too small to conclude.

builder.note: It ran both workflows as declared with no scope drift, no retries and a 12 KB file [10][12]. All 10 done-when items passed on its output.

went_well: Zero redirects, invalid moves, validator refusals, role refusals, pauses or stuck turns. Every hand-off was legal.
The no-invented-facts rule held end to end: Audit passed item 10 and all seven missing facts were tracked as open inputs [15][17].
Priority and Identity were disciplined: Priority left design alone [7], Identity used 3 turns and did not manage the work.
Audit separated what it observed (overflow, JS errors) from what it inferred (tiles) [14][15].
problems: Item 7 (map renders with OSM tiles) was never observed. The mechanical check logged no tile.openstreetmap.org request [15], and Identity accepted it on inference [16].
The 45 spent equals the agent estimates exactly (35, 35, 10, 10), and rate_card is true. It is a billed rate, not measured cost, so estimate accuracy was not tested.
Adaptation sized its work to fit the budget and left no room for a fix [6][7]. Any failed check would have needed a new decision. It never failed, so the cost of that choice is untested.

Done-when mostly tests that content is absent. The Requester gets a page with 7 open inputs. The pause-for-Requester rule never triggered because CEO decision 1 [3] made every item closable without them.
learnings: Test next: a brief or budget that forces a COUNTER, a HOLD or a failed completion check. This run had 0 counters, 0 conflicts, 0 holds and 0 failures, so those paths have no evidence.
Change the test system: capture network requests in the mechanical check (tile and CDN hosts) so map-style items are observed. Also name the 3 external resources it counts.
Change the test system: log real tokens or calls next to the rate-card charge, so Priority's estimates can be compared with actual cost.
Keep: the CEO option shuffle with position logging. Needs many more decisions before it says anything about bias.
Test whether Identity should send one question per ASK_CEO, or whether the format should allow a bundled list. Evidence is one instance [2].
